name: Vesper
title: Shadow Warden
build: Arcane Tankster, adapted for a four-player co-op party
role: The party's front-line tank and thief. In medium armour and a shield she Dashes in, Booming Blades with her Shadow Blade and steps back, so enemies take thunder chasing her. With Braindrain Gloves on, her psychic hits stack Mental Fatigue, setting up her own Phantasmal Killer and Hold Person, and Alene's Hold Person. In Act 3 she wears The Reviving Hands to tank, and swaps Braindrain back in for those fights.
bio: Vesper never knew her parents. The Lower City of Baldur's Gate raised her: its alleys, its rooftops, and the lessons of being a horned girl in a city that crosses the street when it sees one.

By sixteen she was the eldest of the Rats, a handful of orphans who slept in the loft of a burned-out chandlery above the docks. She fed them the way urchins do: lifted purses, emptied lockboxes, and a light touch that never left a trace.

The wards came from a fence's stall. She stole a waterlogged spellbook for the price it would fetch, found it full of abjuration, and kept it instead. Night by night she taught herself to read it: an alarm glyph on the loft's door, a shimmer of force to turn a Flaming Fist cudgel, a blade of shadow for when turning wasn't enough. The kids started calling her their warden. She pretended to hate it.

On the last night, she was on the roof keeping watch when the clouds over the harbour split and something vast slid through them. Tentacles came down into the streets. She remembers shouting for the kids to stay inside, then nothing.
Now she wakes with a worm behind her eyes, on a ship that should not exist, and the Rats are alone in the city. Whatever this is, she's getting back to them.

prepare.note: Once you've scribed Web, swap Hold Person for it when the fight isn't against humanoids. Swap Enhance Leap for Protection from Evil and Good against its creature types. Longstrider is a ritual too: prepare it out of combat and cast it for no slot.

warnings: Neither spell has a scroll, so they can only be learned at level-up. Shadow Blade is essential. Phantasmal Force is optional.

prepare.note: Once you've scribed Web, swap Hold Person for it as needed, or for Phantasmal Force against non-humanoids. At this level you can cast Shadow Blade, then unprepare it.

levels.gains: Shadow Blade: her signature weapon, 2d8 psychic.
levels.play: Big breakpoint. Booming Blade with Shadow Blade, then Sneak Attack, which needs Advantage or an ally next to the target.

choices.label: Feat
choices.text: her melee weapon and Sneak Attack dice each roll twice and keep the higher: about +8 damage per attack with Sneak Attack by level 12, or about +4 without.

choices.label: Or
choices.text: Ability Improvement: +2 Dexterity (DEX becomes 20): +1 AC, to hit, damage, initiative and Sleight of Hand, but about a third of Savage Attacker's damage.

choices.label: Or

warnings: From now on, keep Shadow Blade prepared. Unpreparing it drops an upcast blade to 2d8. Being knocked unconscious loses the blade, so keep a slot to recast it.
Level 3 scribing opens now, but Counterspell's scroll can't be obtained, so it has to wait for level 12.

prepare.note: All her level 3 spells come from scrolls until level 12, so seek out Haste and Glyph of Warding and scribe them. Traders sell them. Casting another concentration spell while Hasted ends the new spell and makes her Lethargic. Swap in Fear, Slow, Hold Person, Hypnotic Pattern, Web or Fireball when the fight calls for it. Glyph of Warding is her area attack: cast on enemies it triggers at once, you pick the damage type, it adds 3 Arcane Ward charges, and it needs no concentration. It can hit her too until Evasion at level 11.

levels.gains: Savage Attacker: her Shadow Blade and Sneak Attack dice roll twice and keep the higher. Level 3 scroll scribing. Shadow Blade reaches 3d8 from a 3rd-level slot.
levels.play: Cast Shadow Blade with a 3rd-level slot.

levels.play: Spotting traps and talking her way out of a caught theft both get much more reliable.

warnings: Mirror Image and Misty Step are now always prepared. Take them out of the Wizard list.

prepare.note: Mirror Image and Misty Step no longer use Wizard spots, so Hold Person and Fear take them. Swap either for Slow when the fight calls for it.

levels.gains: Evasion, Sneak Attack 4d6, and Booming Blade adds 2d8 thunder, and 3d8 when the target moves.
levels.play: Evasion turns many Dexterity-save explosions into no damage.

choices.label: Spells
choices.text: Counterspell is a must. Remove Curse is a flex pick: any level 3 spell you don't know yet.

warnings: Counterspell has no scroll. Don't skip it.

prepare.note: She has one 4th-level slot, so prepare one 4th-level spell: out of combat, swap Phantasmal Killer for Greater Invisibility or Fire Shield if the next fight calls for it. Swap Hold Person for Slow or Fear by fight.

levels.gains: Counterspell, 8 Wizard preparations, and level 4 scroll scribing.
levels.play: Use the one 4th-level slot on Phantasmal Killer, which suits her psychic plan, or whichever 4th-level spell you prepared instead. A 3rd-level slot is enough for Shadow Blade.

illithid.intro: Optional. The build works without the tadpole. She stays off the Astral-Touched Tadpole, so no partial-illithid powers or appearance change: these are the regular powers that fit. Using them means declining the Emperor's tadpole at the end of Act 2 is a DC 21 Wisdom check, and her WIS is 10. Have a party member who has never used a parasite lead that conversation, save first, and test what failing does.
illithid.warning: Awakened turns illithid powers into bonus actions, but her bonus action already goes to Cunning Dash in her hit-and-run turn.

powers.why: Illithid powers cost a bonus action instead of an action. You get it by passing all three saves at the Zaith'isk. Afterwards she can't use illithid powers as actions.

+1d4 psychic on every attack for 10 turns or until combat ends, so each hit adds Mental Fatigue with Braindrain on. Turning it on costs her action until she's Awakened, then her bonus action, so she skips that turn's Booming Blade or Cunning Dash. She takes 1d4 psychic every turn, and Lightning Charges from her Dash can add damage to that hit. It forces a concentration check: best when she isn't holding Phantasmal Killer, Fear or Slow. That damage also strips 2 turns of Arcane Acuity each turn, so it works against the Helmet of Arcane Acuity.
Taken to unlock Cull the Weak and Psionic Backlash.

Finishes off enemies with fewer HP than her number of illithid powers (about 6 here), and each kill deals 1–4 psychic damage to every enemy nearby. With Braindrain Gloves, that spreads Mental Fatigue across the group.

Cast it before the fight: 10 temporary HP that last until a long rest. When opportunity attacks break it, it bursts, and enemies within 3 m make a DC 15 INT save or are Stunned for a turn. Mental Fatigue lowers that save. Stunned enemies lose their next turn and their concentration, and friends who act before then get Advantage, but the stun probably ends before her next attack: test the timing. She can only hold temporary HP from one source, and sources disagree on what Vivacious Cloak's 8 would do: it may replace the shield with no burst, or do nothing. Test this in game before relying on the Stun.

A reaction when an enemy within 9 m casts a spell: 1d4 psychic per spell level, which adds Mental Fatigue with Braindrain on and can break their concentration. It uses the reaction she'd spend on Shield or Counterspell, so save it for fights against casters.

The spell's blade is lost if she's knocked unconscious; check whether the ring's is too. Every instance of psychic damage she deals adds 2 turns of Mental Fatigue: every Shadow Blade hit, Psionic Overload on bow shots, Cull the Weak's splash on every nearby enemy and Psionic Backlash. A failed mental save at 5 or more turns clears it for 1d4 psychic, so it sets up one save per target. Her main until Act 3, then her swap for fights she leads with Phantasmal Killer or Hold Person, or sets up Alene's Hold Person.

Her Act 3 gloves. Healing herself gives her Blade Ward, and the Helm of Balduran's heal does that at the start of each of her turns in combat. Sold by Vicar Humbletoes in the Lower City.

gear.claim: Vesper (decided).

Summoned by her Shadow Blade spell. Cast with a 3rd-level slot for 3d8 psychic.

loop.title: Dash in
loop.text: Cunning Action: Dash toward the target. The Speedy Lightfeet give 3 Lightning Charges.

loop.title: Strike
loop.text: Booming Blade with Shadow Blade, and add Sneak Attack on the hit if she has Advantage or an ally, such as the Hand, is next to the target.

loop.title: Back out
loop.text: Use the rest of her movement to back away, so the target has to move to reach her and takes Booming Blade's thunder.

situations.title: Taking opportunity attacks
situations.text: Backing away draws opportunity attacks. Uncanny Dodge halves each hit and, in the current patch, doesn't use up her reaction, so Shield (+5 AC for the round) and Counterspell stay free. The Arcane Ward soaks the rest. Misses trigger Holy Lance Helm and the Adamantine Shield.

situations.title: Arcane Ward is empty
situations.text: An empty Arcane Ward refills to her Wizard level the next time she casts Booming Blade or gains Lightning Charges or Arcane Acuity. It only works at exactly 0 charges. The wiki lists this refill as a bug, so a patch could remove it.

situations.title: Can't reach the target
situations.text: Can't reach a target? Cast Blade Ward and Dash past enemies instead: resistance plus Uncanny Dodge cuts their physical hits by 75%.

situations.title: Dash is too risky
situations.text: If an opportunity attack would be too dangerous, use Cunning Disengage instead of Dash.

situations.title: Bombs
situations.text: Bombs are a last resort. From level 11, Evasion makes point-blank bombs much safer for her, but not for her friends. Before one, fill her Arcane Ward and boost her saves with Bless or Resistance.

situations.title: Friends' area spells
situations.text: From level 11, Evasion means a passed DEX save takes no damage from Alene's Call Lightning or Ice Storm, Pearl's Conjure Barrage, Glyph of Warding, Fireball and most grenades, so friends can aim them at enemies around her. Smokepowder Arrows aren't covered, and the wiki doesn't list Spike Growth, Hunger of Hadar, Cone of Cold, Sunbeam, Insect Plague or Wall of Fire.

start_of_day: Cast Longstrider: more movement for running in and back out.
Prepare the Wizard spells for her level, then swap freely out of combat.
From level 8, cast Shadow Blade. From level 9, use a 3rd-level slot.
Before a theft: Boon ring, cast Disguise Self, then theft ring and gloves.
Decide whether the Resonance Stone is safe to carry today.

theft.title: Get ready
steps: Put on Shapeshifter's Boon Ring, then cast Disguise Self (from level 11, use Mask of the Shapeshifter).
Put on Smuggler's Ring and Gloves of Thievery, and from Act 2 Cloak of Cunning Brume. Get Guidance from Alene, or cast it with the Silver Pendant.

theft.title: The lift
steps: Split from the group and Hide. Keep your friends out of the crime scene.

From Act 2: Disengage next to the target in Cloak of Cunning Brume, then switch to turn-based mode, Hide in the fog and pickpocket before it fades after 1 turn. Test this first with nobody around: the wiki now says the fog only appears in combat. If there's no fog, shoot a Darkness arrow next to the target instead, as in Act 1.
Steal at least one copy of every Wizard scroll you find.
After a successful pickpocket, leave before the victim notices.

theft.title: If it goes wrong
steps: If caught and given a dialogue check, pick Deception. Use Friends after a failed pickpocket, once Guidance doesn't matter any more (untested: the target may react before she can cast it). On Tactician, casting Friends is itself a crime, so cast it out of sight.
On Tactician, Friends can anger its target when it ends. Leave, camp or fast-travel before the 10 turns run out. Never use Friends on companions.
Caught with no dialogue check: Disengage for fog, or shoot a Darkness arrow for a longer-lasting cloud, then Hide in it and get away.
Next time, use a different disguise: the victim shouldn't recognise her (untested).
If you keep getting caught, slip away instead of escalating.

reactions.name: Sneak Attack
reactions.why: Booming Blade is her only attack on her own turn, so there's no better hit to save it for. It's once per round and refreshes after her turn, so an opportunity attack on an enemy's turn can use it, but then it won't be there on her next turn. Check in game that it leaves her reaction free.

reactions.name: Sneak Attack (Critical Hit)
reactions.why: The same on a crit, with the dice doubled. With Sarevok's helmet swapped in, she crits on 19–20.

reactions.name: Shield
reactions.why: Spend the slot only when +5 AC changes the result. It gives no Arcane Ward charges.

reactions.name: Counterspell
reactions.why: Skip harmless casts. It always gives 3 Arcane Ward charges.

reactions.name: Hellish Rebuke
reactions.why: Low priority: weak with her Charisma.

reactions.name: Uncanny Dodge
reactions.why: A toggled passive, on by default, not a Reactions tab setting. Halves each hit from a different attacker. In the current patch it needs her reaction unspent but doesn't use it up, so Shield and Counterspell stay available, though spending her reaction on them switches it off until it returns.

reactions.name: Rebuke of the Mighty (Viconia's)
reactions.why: Never let it take the reaction you need for Shield or Counterspell.

mage_hand.title: Scout
mage_hand.text: Scout dangerous rooms while it's invisible. It turns visible when it acts and goes invisible again on a short rest.

mage_hand.title: Potion courier
mage_hand.text: Drop a potion for the Hand to throw to an ally.

mage_hand.title: Flanking buddy
mage_hand.text: Stand it next to an enemy to count as the ally Sneak Attack needs.

mage_hand.title: Lights out
mage_hand.text: Turn off lights so targets are obscured, which gives her Shadow Blade Advantage (untested: the wiki doesn't confirm the Hand can do this).

mage_hand.title: Ledge shove
mage_hand.text: Before combat, throw or shove enemies off ledges or into chasms. Give the Hand a Hill Giant Strength elixir first so the throw succeeds.

mage_hand.title: Keep it alive
mage_hand.text: Cast Mage Armour and Longstrider on the Hand to keep it alive and moving. Mage Armour must stay prepared, or come from a scroll.
